unreleased: The Terms no longer say the price may carry the user's country's VAT when the provider is not a VAT payer: that sentence now follows the provider's VAT status (a non-payer states that the price is final and nothing is added to it), and the Privacy page says the country of the billing address is kept with each payment.

Add a tickets module (src/modules/tickets) for administrators: a list of tickets (search by number, title or requester, filters by status and type, paging) with the mailbox status and a Check mail now button, a form to open a ticket by hand (type, requester, optional CRM partner picker, description), and a ticket page with a header (title, type, total time, requester, partner linked to the CRM, close / reopen), the thread of notes and mails and a form below it: a rich-text editor with pictures, file attachments, the time spent (90, 1:30, 1h 30m) and a switch between an internal note and an e-mail to the requester. A CRM partner's page lists the partner's tickets (a new "crm.partner" slot in the CRM, which the tickets module fills); a header icon links to the tickets for administrators. Czech and English

Search engines find the site better: robots.txt is now generated by the build with an absolute link to the sitemap and lists the pages that really are private (the old one named pages that do not exist and linked the sitemap with a relative address); descriptions are tidied and cut at a word to about 160 characters; the home page, the category list and every category carry structured data (WebSite, CollectionPage, breadcrumbs); Twitter card tags are filled in; and index.html itself now says what the site is (description, Open Graph, theme colour, a text for visitors without JavaScript), which is all that link previews see. My posts, My payments, My receipts, Moderation, New category, a category that does not exist, the 404 page and search results are marked noindex, and the 404 image has an alt text

Search the categories: a search box above the list on the home page and on /categories finds categories by words in the title or description, ignoring case and diacritics ("priroda" finds "Příroda"), after you stop typing, with a count of what was found, a message and a "Clear search" link when nothing matches, and the same "Load more". The list says it is ordered by the number of posts, busiest first, and stays so when searching. On /categories the search is in the address (?q=), so it can be shared and survives a reload

The application is now called BumpFeel (it was ThoughtAuction, in Czech "Aukce myšlenek"): the page title, the header, the home page, the Terms and the Privacy policy carry the new name in both languages

Add an event_booking module (src/modules/event_booking) for registering for an event: a Register button under each date of an article (the dates of an event with a registration), which opens a form - pick a day from a list or from a month calendar in which only days with a free place can be chosen, then a time where the day has times, then name, e-mail, consent to the processing of personal data and the questions of the form (usable at 320 px, light and dark); a registration for signed-in visitors only asks you to sign in and brings you back to the article afterwards (a small helper for returning to a page after signing in, also used by the Google sign-in and the consent step), and one reached by a secret link appears only when the page was opened with it. The link in the confirmation e-mail opens a page with a Cancel button. For administrators: the registrations of all events, an editor of one (details, who may register, a link to copy and renew, blocks of days and times with a live preview of the slots they offer, the form's questions, the bookings, a CSV export, a purge of old bookings), and in the editor of an event a Registration panel with the table of its bookings - to open one, see its answers and history of changes, move it, correct its name, e-mail or answers, or cancel it, each with a note and an e-mail to the person - and a summary of the answers of confirmed bookings

Add a forms module (src/modules/forms): an editor of a form's questions (seven types, options, limits, a pattern, and conditions that show a question only for certain earlier answers), the visitor's form in which questions appear and disappear as it is answered, and for administrators a list of the answers, a page with one answer in full, and a summary per question with bars, counts and shares (how many saw a conditional question and how many answered, averages of numbers, earliest and latest dates). Other modules embed these; the page /forms/manage/<form id> shows all the answers of a form

Fix the application failing to start (a blank page with "Cannot access 'default' before initialization" in the console) when a page imports something from a module before the module registry is loaded, as an application's home page does with the event calendar: the list of enabled modules now lives in its own file that no module has to import the registry for

The event calendar now builds on articles: an event is a date (or a run of days, with optional times) of an article and leads to it - there is no separate event page any more. The calendar colours days and events by the article's type (light and dark theme), marks pinned articles with a pin and shows an event's short description (up to 128 characters) when you point at it or tab to it, with its popup kept on screen on phones. An article's page lists its dates, an article's editor has a panel to add, edit and delete them, and the administrators' date form picks the article by searching. Other modules can add to these pages through three new slots (event.actions, event.manage, event.editor)

Add an articles module (src/modules/articles): a list with search and a type filter, the article page drawn in its type's colours (light and dark theme), and an administrator area to write articles with the full editor (images, video, tables, HTML source), choose status and display window, pin them and manage the article types and their colours
The rich-text editor gains text alignment, tables, a horizontal rule, code blocks, YouTube / Vimeo video links and an HTML source mode (the server still strips anything unsafe on save)

A module can declare the modules it requires (a console warning is logged once when one is enabled without them) and contribute components to named slots that other modules render with <ModuleSlot>, so a module can extend another module's pages without that module knowing about it

The "New category" button is shown to administrators only, and the new-category page tells everybody else that only an administrator can create a category (and that they can still add posts to the existing ones); the Terms say so too

The release build no longer writes its own frontend .env with fixed addresses: it copies the development directory's frontend/.env as it is stored, stops with guidance when it is missing, and warns when an address in it points at localhost

Page titles and descriptions no longer say "Authenticate WFB": every page now takes the application's name (nav.brand) and a default description (meta.description) from its translations, and also sets a canonical URL, Open Graph and Twitter tags and the page language. Sign-in, account, administration and diagnostic pages ask search engines not to index them

The contact page can now show an introduction, contact details (email, address, GitHub, LinkedIn) and a note next to the form, all set per deployment; the page moved to /contact (/kontakt redirects there). With nothing configured it is still just the form

Add a CRM module (src/modules/crm), shown to administrators only: a header icon opens the partner list with search, each partner's page with their tasks, and each task's page where invoice PDFs are uploaded, downloaded and deleted - in Czech and English

Fix the header on phones when signed in: the app name wrapped and its small tag slid under the notification bell. The header is now more compact on small screens, the name truncates (and gives way to the logo alone on the narrowest phones), and the tag only shows from tablet width up

The Terms now say that a post's value never falls below zero: a post whose age outweighs what was paid for it and its resonances is worth 0, and each further resonance or payment is then added to zero and shows in full

The moderation page warns administrators when payments are off: a notice above the tabs says why no author is offered a payment (the gateway module is not enabled, a Stripe key is missing, or the provider's details are incomplete - naming the blank fields) and reminds them to restart the backend after changing the settings. It is not shown while payments are on

You can pay for a new post in the same step as publishing it: where payments are on, the new-post form has an optional "Raise its value right away" amount (quick $5 / $10 / $25 or any whole number of USD, with the points it buys), the consent to immediate performance and the terms notice, and the button becomes "Publish and pay $N". The post is checked and published first, then you are taken to Stripe; if you abandon the payment or it cannot be started, the post stays published and you can raise its value later (the offer appears right below the form). The "Raise value" payment button now matches the rest of the page

You can hide your own post and show it again: a "Hide" button on your post on the board (it asks first, then the post leaves the board) and on "My posts", where a hidden post is labelled "Hidden", explains that its value keeps falling with age while nobody can see it, and has a "Show again" button. The Terms now say so too, and "My payments" tells you when the post a payment went to is hidden

A new look, light and dark: every post is its own card on a leaderboard - gold, silver and bronze medals for the first three, rank numbers below, the value as a big score, and after each refresh an arrow showing how many places a post climbed or lost; the category page opens with a banner, categories are tiles, and the forms, "My posts", "My payments" and "My receipts" follow suit. The header gets "My posts" and "My payments" buttons (shown when you are signed in), and the menu items are now pills with the current page highlighted
The "Add a post" button and the Cancel button on a category page are now translated into English (they showed the Czech text for English readers)

A category's posts now refresh by themselves, so you can watch the order change: the list is fetched again every minute while the tab is visible (as many posts as you have scrolled through, replacing what is shown), at once when you come back to a tab that was in the background, and right after you click "Resonate", so the post takes its new place immediately. A small line above the list says when it was last updated

The Terms now say that an administrator can block a whole category (its posts are hidden, not deleted or counted as violating, and keep what was paid) and that a block - of a post or of a category - can be withdrawn, which publishes the post or the category again and stops it counting towards the account limit

A new "My payments" page shows the total you have paid and every payment for your posts - which post, when, its status, what the post is now (blocked and removed posts say the amount is not refunded) - with a link to each payment's document, which opens on the receipts page. "My posts" and "My receipts" link to it

Moderation posts have a "Restore" button for blocked and removed posts (the author is notified, and told it was restored); if the author's account is blocked it says to unblock the account first. The blocked-accounts tab now points to it for the posts removed with an account

Moderation has a new "Categories" tab: every category, blocked ones too, searchable, with a button to block one (with a reason its creator is sent) and one to restore it. A post in a blocked category shows on "My posts" as hidden, with an explanation, and cannot be boosted; the creator gets the block and the restore as notifications

A new "My receipts" page lists the documents for your payments and shows each one exactly as it was emailed, in your language; the terms and the privacy policy now say that a confirmation of the contract and a payment document are emailed after each payment and are also available in the app

Pay to raise a post's value: your own posts show "Your post" with what you have paid and a "Raise value" button that opens a panel for a whole number of USD (with the points it buys, and the required consent to immediate performance) and sends you to Stripe; right after publishing a post you are offered the same. The result page returns you to the board with the new value. A new "My posts" page lists your anonymous posts in every state, with their value, what you paid, and why one was blocked

Add the Terms ("Pravidla a podmínky"), Privacy policy (GDPR), About and Cookies pages for BumpFeel, linked from the footer, with the content rules, how checks and blocking work, anonymity of authors, the value formula and the payment terms - the numbers in them come from the new `params` in public/legal.json - and the Contact page in the header; the post and category forms, the check verdicts and the blocked-account notice now link to the rules and the contact form

Boards moderation in the UI: publishing a post or a category now checks it first and shows the verdict before anything is published - a warning to edit above 30 %, a potential risk to confirm ("Publish anyway") above 50 %, a refusal above 75 % - with the specific reasons and the words they were found in (and, for a post that does not fit its category, what the category is about); a blocked account sees why instead of the form; and a /moderation page for administrators to find and block posts with a reason, edit or rebuild a category's machine rules and unblock accounts. Authors get a notification when a post of theirs is blocked
The home page now introduces BumpFeel and lists the categories, and the page title and meta description carry the BumpFeel name instead of the template's

Add a boards module (src/modules/boards): a "Categories" nav link to the list of categories, a page per category with its posts ordered by value and loaded endlessly as you scroll (plain bold title and text, value and resonance count, no author), a form to add a post (title and text up to 2048 characters, with an emoji row and live character counters) and a Resonate button for signed-in users, and a page to create a category
